script.title: Chapter 4: The Fishermen of the Pepper Coast

panels.description: Wide, full page width. A storm-spent sea under a flat grey sky, long heavy swells breaking on a shallow curve of beach. Black rock outcrops break the sand. Small in the foam, Nagoji is thrown face down onto the beach, one arm flung out. Floating timber in the surf behind him. No other people anywhere. No irons, manacles, chain or collar on him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: When the sea finally spat me out, it did so without ceremony.

panels.description: Ground level, tight. Nagoji's hands dug into coarse wet grit: the fingers wrapped in soaked, filthy bandage, the heels of the palms bare and raw with rope burn, the wrist bandages sodden and slipping. His left forearm is crusted with wet sand; no mark on it is readable yet. The retreating surf drags at his legs in the background. He is in the captivity rags, sodden: torn ochre sleeveless tunic, ripped open down the front, cream dhoti. Two loops of rope are still knotted across his chest under the armpits, well clear of the neck, the frayed free end trailing into the foam. Raw chafe rings at the ankles where iron once bit. No ankle irons, no manacles, no chain, no neck collar.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Breathing was a battle. Each time I drew in air it brought more salt, more pain.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's face, cheek pressed to wet sand, one eye half open, long curly black hair plastered across it. Thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN (faint stubble shadow at most, no beard), small gold ear stud, no turban. A thin sheet of wave washes over his shoulder and back. His left arm is out of frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My limbs felt like they belonged to someone else, a man made of lead and bruises.

panels.description: Full width, bottom strip. Same low angle along the sand, but the tide line has moved and the light has shifted: time has passed. At the far edge of the panel, three pairs of bare brown feet are approaching over the sand, leaving prints. We see no more of them than that.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The sea was no longer alone.

copy.speaker: VOICE (off)
copy.text: ...alive...

copy.speaker: VOICE (off)
copy.text: Look at his hands...

copy.speaker: VOICE (off)
copy.text: See the brand on his arm.

panels.description: Nagoji's point of view, flat on his back, looking straight up. A lowering grey sky, the colour of stale rice water. Three faces close the frame around it like a ring, framed by beards and damp hair, sun-and-salt brown skin. Faces, hair and beards only in this panel; the costumes are established in 2.4. Establish the three faces now and hold them for the chapter. **FISHERMAN**: forties, the leader, broad face, short grizzled beard, strong white teeth, the edge of a white cotton cloth on his LEFT shoulder. **YOUNG FISHERMAN**: twenties, slim face, thin black beard, quick eyes, a cloth tied round his head as a headband. **WARY FISHERMAN**: older and gaunt, long grey-streaked beard, the coil of a net on his shoulder, leaning in least, already half turned away.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They were not Portuguese.

panels.description: The Fisherman (short grizzled beard, shoulder cloth) pushes Nagoji's hair back from his forehead with rough fingers. Nagoji flinches, one bandaged hand half rising to guard his face. Habit, not fear. The rope loops are still across his chest; his left forearm stays sand-caked, no mark readable. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: Easy, *bhau*. You are on land now.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: *Bhau.* Brother, in Konkani. Near enough to my Marathi.

panels.description: Tight. A clay pot pressed to Nagoji's cracked lips, water spilling down his clean-shaven chin and moustache. No beard.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Water.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The first swallow burned. The second soothed.

panels.description: Wide, from just behind Nagoji's left shoulder as he props himself on his left elbow and looks past the men; his left forearm lies flat on the sand, inner side down. In the middle ground the three fishermen stand at full figure, so their costume reads; hold it for the chapter. All barefoot, lungis hitched up to the thigh, short sleeveless vests clinging wet. FISHERMAN: stocky, faded madder-red lungi, cream vest, white cotton cloth over his LEFT shoulder. YOUNG FISHERMAN: slim, indigo lungi, faded blue vest, cloth headband, sliding a short fishing knife back into his waist-knot; beside Nagoji on the sand lie the rope loops he has just cut away. WARY FISHERMAN: gaunt, undyed off-white lungi, dark brown vest, a coiled net over one shoulder. Beyond them: the shallow curve of beach, black rock, a line of coconut palms with fronds bent in the wind. On the sand to the right, the broken carcass of a ship's boat, planks scattered. Farther along the shore, half hidden in spray, the same black, high-sided ship from chapters 2 and 3, carved stern castle, mainmast snapped, heeled over and cracked open on a reef offshore. Timber bobbing in the surf. From here on, no rope on Nagoji, and no irons, manacles, chain or collar.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I recognised the curve of a Portuguese hull.

panels.description: Narrow strip. Nagoji's point of view along the surf line, left to right: foam, floating planks, a torn scrap of sail. No human figure anywhere, in the water or on the sand. At most, a sliver of Nagoji's cheek and eye at the left edge of the foreground.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: No bodies. Not that I could see.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Perhaps the sea had decided it had eaten enough men for one day.

panels.description: Wide. Nagoji half sitting, centre, the torn ochre tunic hanging open over raw rope burns on his chest; no rope on him. The Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) kneels at Nagoji's RIGHT and turns up his right hand: the bandage wraps only the fingers, and the heel of the palm is bare, hard with rein and sword calluses and raw with fresh rope burn. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) kneels at Nagoji's LEFT, turns the left forearm over and scrapes a crust of wet sand off its inner side with his thumb, just above the slipping wrist bandage. What he uncovers is not yet readable at this distance. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: YOUNG FISHERMAN
copy.text: <He has soldier's calluses. Not a clerk. Not a merchant.>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <Look at this.>

panels.description: Insert, tight, generated as its own close-up rather than cropped from a wider frame. The Portuguese brand on the inner side of Nagoji's LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist: a short row of raised, ridged burn scars, puckered and angry, crude marks blurred past reading. No legible letters, no numerals, no cross. The Fisherman's sandy thumb at the edge of frame, wet sand just scraped from around the mark. The soaked edge of the wrist bandage below it.
The Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, net on shoulder) stands apart, ankle-deep at the tide line, glancing up the coast toward the wreck and then back at the others. He wants to be anywhere else.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They argued in Malayalam. I could not follow a word. I did not need to.

copy.speaker: WARY FISHERMAN
copy.text: <Kill him. Why bring trouble to the village?>

copy.speaker: WARY FISHERMAN
copy.text: <The Portuguese will send men for their ship. Better the sea finishes its work.>

panels.description: The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth), still crouched at Nagoji's side, snorts and turns his head to the Wary Fisherman. The posture of a man haggling at a fish market.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <The Portuguese and the Dutch ask questions anyway.>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <You think leaving one marata on the sand will satisfy either of them?>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <We might as well gain something.>

panels.description: The Fisherman turns back to Nagoji and leans in, close. The look of a man doing sums. Nagoji meets his eyes. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: WARY FISHERMAN (off)
copy.text: <What? He is half dead.>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <Half is still half.>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: You fought them, yes?

panels.description: Wide, resetting the geography with every figure at full scale. Nagoji up on one elbow on the sand, water still running from his hair. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) crouched at his side; the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) standing over them; the Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, net) a few paces off, already turned toward the palms. The wreck in the surf behind. Nagoji's voice is a rasp but his eyes are steady. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache; no irons, manacles, chain or collar.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes. On the Deccan roads. Near their forts.

panels.description: The Fisherman nods once, as if a calculation has come out right, and jerks his chin south down the coast. The line of palms runs away into haze.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: Our king to the south fights them too. And the other pale ones from the north, the Dutch.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: He sharpens his teeth for them.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: A man who has seen Portuguese dungeons and still breathes may be useful.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji. Something wakes behind the exhaustion. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache, gold ear stud.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: King. Teeth. Dutch. The words caught like hooks.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Travancore.

panels.description: Two-shot. The Fisherman's brows go up. Nagoji, still propped on one elbow, back straight, chin lifted, shoulders squared despite the exhaustion. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: You know the name.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I know they have not yet learned to kneel when a foreign flag flies.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That is enough.

panels.description: Full width. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) grins, teeth white against weathered skin, as he takes Nagoji's shoulders; the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) takes his legs; the Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, net) is already walking ahead, scanning the shore. In the foreground, a small sand crab sidles out of the way. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard; no irons, manacles, chain or collar.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: You see, he has a tongue as well as scars.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: Come, *bhau*. Before the crabs claim you.

panels.description: Wide, high angle from up among the first coconut palms, looking back down the slope toward the sea. The carry party climbs toward us: the Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, net) leading, the Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) carrying Nagoji's shoulders, the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) his legs. Nagoji slung between them, head tipped back, eyes on the fronds. Behind and below them: the empty beach, the ship's boat lying untouched on the sand, and the wreck small and far off on its reef. Nobody is stripping it. No irons or chains on Nagoji.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The smell of earth instead of salt.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: After the dungeon and the storm, these small things felt like gifts.

panels.description: Wide. The village beyond the palms: narrow paths between wet paddy, low houses of mud and red laterite stone with palm-thatch roofs. Children stare from doorways. Village women in plain mundu with an upper cloth draped over both shoulders, modestly covered, water pots on their hips, have stopped on the path. In the foreground, a small girl whispers to the child beside her, eyes on Nagoji, the dripping stranger carried between the fishermen in the middle distance.

copy.speaker: GIRL
copy.text: <Portuguese.>

panels.description: The Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband), carrying Nagoji's legs, turns his head sharply toward the girl. The girl shrinks back. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) holds Nagoji's shoulders at the far end. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache; no irons or chains.

copy.speaker: YOUNG FISHERMAN
copy.text: <No. Look at his eyes. Look at his mark.>

copy.speaker: YOUNG FISHERMAN
copy.text: <This one is enemy of the Portuguese.>

panels.description: A low house at the edge of the village. The Woman steps out of the doorway, wiping her hands on her cloth: heavy-set, in her fifties, hair in a loose low knot heavily streaked with grey, betel-stained lips, no gold, no walking stick, coarse undyed cotton worn sari-fashion with the end drawn over both shoulders, no fitted blouse. One frozen moment: a faint betel-stained half-smile at the corner of her mouth, her gaze fixed on the brand. Nagoji, held between the carriers, has his LEFT forearm turned toward camera across his body so the brand on its inner side shows; the torn tunic hangs open over the raw rope burns on his chest. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) beside her, mid-gesture, talking. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard; no irons or chains.

copy.speaker: WOMAN
copy.text: <Bring him in.>

copy.speaker: WOMAN
copy.text: <If he dies, burn him quietly. Otherwise, send word to the *kapitan*.>

panels.description: Interior, cool and dim. Packed earth floor swept smooth; smoke from a small hearth curling up toward a hole in the thatch. Nagoji on a woven mat, the salt-stiff tunic peeled off and set aside, the cream dhoti left on him; rope burns across his chest; the brand on his left inner forearm. The Woman (grey-streaked low knot, undyed cotton) washes him with a cloth and a clay basin, brisk rather than gentle. She has unwound the bandage from one hand. Frame it so his fingers are turned away from us or lost in her shadow: we read the damage only in her face, her mouth pulled tight. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) squats at the mat's edge. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache; no irons or chains.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: She asks what they did to you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Asked questions.

panels.description: The Woman (grey-streaked low knot, undyed cotton) clicks her tongue and wrings the cloth hard into the basin, speaking fast and sharp at no one in particular. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) relays it with half a smile. Nagoji on the mat in the foreground.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: She says keep your stories for the *kapitan*.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: She does not need to hear them to know what kind of men they are.

panels.description: A boy in the doorway, backlit by grey daylight, panting, one hand on the frame, talking fast. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) and the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) exchange a look across the room.

copy.speaker: BOY
copy.text: ... *kapitan* ... *kapitan* ...

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: So. I was not the first piece of foreign wreckage to wash up in their nets.

panels.description: The Fisherman (red lungi), crouched by the mat, adjusts the white cotton cloth on his own left shoulder (the one established in 2.1), voice low. Nagoji on the mat, looking up at him. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: Rest. When the *kapitan* comes, speak carefully.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: He works for men who have long arms.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Storms on land were different from storms at sea. They did not roar and crash; they crept in on quiet feet, through conversations and calculations.

panels.description: Full-width tier, not a narrow strip. Nagoji's eyes closed, hearth light on his face. Behind him, out of focus, the Fisherman and the Young Fisherman are turning their heads toward the door, straightening, and a broad shadow falls across the swept floor. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had escaped the Portuguese dungeon and the drowning ship by chance and stubbornness.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: If I was to survive whatever came next, I would need more than that.

panels.description: Large, about the bottom 40 percent of the page. Camera low, from beside Nagoji's mat, looking up. The *kapitan* has stepped a pace inside so his face is in the room: three-quarter view with HIS OWN (anatomical) left cheek toward camera, lit warm by the hearth; the scar runs from that left ear to the corner of his jaw. Grey daylight from the doorway only rims his shoulders. Shorter than the fishermen but broader: the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) stands just behind him, half a head taller, drawing back with respect beside the Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth). White turban, short grey-flecked beard, pale vest over a white mundu. No coat (the coat arrives in chapter 6). He says nothing. A slow, appraising look moves over the brand, the hands, the shoulders; Nagoji's left forearm lies on the mat, inner side up, toward him. Nagoji, on the mat in the foreground, has opened his eyes and is looking straight back. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache; no irons or chains.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His eyes moved over me the way a horse trader's eyes move over new stock.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had seen that look before, in market squares where men were sold.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In that silence, I was being weighed.

frames.review_note: v02 is clean. It is a wide storm-grey beach with black rock outcrops and timber in the surf. Nagoji lies small and face down in the foam with his arms flung out and bandaged wrists, and a frayed rope end trails from him, which matches 1.2. There are no irons, chain or collar, and plenty of empty sky for the caption. v01 is not acceptable. It crops Nagoji large in the foreground rather than small in the foam, which breaks the wide establishing beat. It also leaves his hands and wrists unbandaged, which contradicts the bandaged fingers in 1.2.

Minor issues only. The framing is a medium shot with his face included rather than a tight ground-level shot of the hands, and the palms are pressed down, so the raw heels of the palms do not show. Otherwise the beat is correct: bandaged fingers dug into coarse grit, slipping wrist bandages and a sand-crusted left forearm with no mark. The rope loops sit across the chest under the armpits, clear of the neck, with the frayed end in the foam. There is a reddish chafe ring at the ankle, no irons, a moustache, a gold ear stud and an ochre tunic with a cream dhoti. The caption has room in the sky at top right. v02 has the cleaner chin. v01 is the same image with slightly heavier stubble, which is still within 'light stubble at most', so it is the backup.

Minor only. The right side of the moustache droops down toward the sand instead of curling up, which reads as wet hair pressed flat, not a beard. The cheek and jaw are clean and the chin is pressed into the sand. The shoulder and back mass is soft but reads as a man lying face down. The rope loops on the torso sit on the shoulder and ribs, well clear of the neck, which matches 1.2. The caption fits over the grey sky and distant surf at the top left, clear of the face.

In v01 the lower legs run up to about knee height at the top edge, behind where the balloons sit. Nothing else of the men shows. The light shifts to a low sun breaking under grey storm cloud, which still sits well beside the grey sky of 2.1. Otherwise it matches the beat: the same low angle along the sand, a moved tide line, and three pairs of bare brown feet walking in from the right edge and leaving a trail of prints. Toe counts and anatomy are sound, and the open sky at left and centre takes the caption and the off-panel voices. Rejected: v02 has only five feet, and the legs are cut off by a hard horizontal line under the balloon. v03 has five disembodied feet ending at the ankle in mid-air. v04 shows only two pairs of legs. v06 shows four feet stacked in a column with no legs. v05 is the backup: three sound pairs of feet, but they stand still in the shallows rather than approaching with a trail of prints, and there is no horizon or sky to show the time shift.

Minor only: the Young Fisherman is drawn upside down (he leans in from behind Nagoji's head), which fits the flat-on-back POV but makes his face slightly harder to read; his faded blue vest shows a little although the script keeps costume for 2.4, and it matches the 2.4 costume. Leader (short grizzled beard, white teeth, cloth on his left shoulder) and Wary Fisherman (long grey-streaked beard, net coil, looking away) match. No text, clean grey sky at centre-bottom for the caption.

Minor: the Fisherman's white cloth drapes over his near (right) shoulder rather than the left named for 2.1 and 2.4; the script for 2.2 does not fix a side. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and gold ear stud, and he flinches with a bandaged hand half raised. The rope loops are across his chest, his left forearm is out of frame, and the fisherman's rough fingers push his hair back. The stormy beach and grey sky match page 1. No painted balloons or text. The sky at top right (above the rocks) takes the Fisherman balloon, and the top-left sky or the low-detail dhoti cloth at bottom left takes the caption.

v02 is acceptable. Water pours from a clay pot into Nagoji's mouth and runs down his clean-shaven chin. His moustache and gold stud match the sheet, rope burns show on his chest, and the background is empty surf. A fisherman's brown arm and cream vest are visible, and the second hand under the pot is plausible. The framing is a medium close-up rather than truly tight, and the pot pours at his lips rather than being pressed to them. That is acceptable. No rope is visible on the chest, which fits because 2.4 shows the rope already cut away. Rejected v01: Portuguese soldiers in morions stand in the background with a fort, the pot is held by a man in a European doublet and belt (the beat is 'They were not Portuguese'), and the brand is shown on his forearm too early.

v02 and v03 are essentially the same image, with pixel differences of under 1 percent. All three fishermen stand at full figure in the scripted costumes. The Fisherman wears a madder-red lungi and a cream vest, with the white cloth on his LEFT shoulder. The Young Fisherman wears an indigo lungi, a blue vest and a headband, and is sheathing a short knife at his waist-knot. The Wary Fisherman wears an off-white lungi and a dark brown vest, with a coiled net and clay floats. The cut rope loops lie on the sand, the broken ship's boat is at right, the black high-sided wreck with a carved stern and broken masts is on the reef, and palms and black rocks fill the shore. The caption area in the sky is clear. Caveats: the Fisherman's beard reads as a moustache with grizzled stubble, lighter than in 2.2. The foreground forearm is probably Nagoji's right, not the scripted left, but it lies outer side up with a sand crust and no readable mark, so the brand stays hidden as intended. Rejected v01: Nagoji's hand has no bandage.

v01 is clean. It is a narrow surf-line strip of foam, floating planks and a torn scrap of sail on a spar, with black rocks at right matching the rest of the page. No human figure appears anywhere, and two clear sky areas take the two captions. Rejected v02: the bottom third of the frame is a blank white area, so the image is broken.

Minor only. The wreck sits beached at the left edge instead of offshore on the reef (per 2.4), so it does not match its offshore position in 3.3. Nagoji's left foot has bandaged toes, which the script does not call for. The Young Fisherman's vest is deep indigo rather than faded blue. Nagoji is on-model: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, open ochre tunic, rope burns on his chest, no rope. Both fishermen are on the correct sides and doing the right actions, and the forearm mark is not yet readable. There is no text. Lettering space: sky top-left above the wreck for the Young Fisherman's line, and sky between Nagoji's and the Fisherman's heads for 'Look at this.'

Clean. This is a real tight insert, not a crop. The brand on the inner forearm, above the soaked wrist bandage, is a puckered patch of ridged scar tissue with no legible letters, numerals or cross, and no blood. The Fisherman's sandy thumb is scraping wet sand at the left edge. The ochre tunic, cream dhoti and grey surf behind match 3.1. No lettering needed.

Minor only. The Wary Fisherman stands closer to shin-deep in the surf than ankle-deep at the tide line. The wreck is offshore on the right, where 3.1 had it beached on the left. He matches his 2.1/2.4 design (gaunt, long grey-streaked beard, dark brown vest, off-white lungi, net coil on his shoulder), stands alone, and glances up the coast toward the wreck. Hands and legs are sound, with no text. The large open sky top-left and centre holds the caption and both balloons.

Acceptable with minor continuity drift. (1) The brand on Nagoji's LEFT forearm is a darkish, looping, tattoo-like smudge on the visible upper side of the mid-forearm, not the pale puckered patch on the inner forearm shown in 3.2. It is unreadable, with no letters, numerals or cross, and it is small at reading size. A retouch to lighten it into a pale ridged scar would tidy it. (2) The bandages wrap Nagoji's wrists and the backs of his hands, leaving the fingers bare, the reverse of 3.1's finger wraps. This is close to 3.5's treatment. (3) Light stubble shadow on the chin, within the bible's allowance. The beat is right: the Fisherman (grizzled beard, grey-streaked curls, bare head, cream vest, white cloth on his own LEFT shoulder, madder-red lungi) crouches at Nagoji's side. He has turned his head and his open-palmed haggling hand toward the Wary Fisherman, who stands small and apart at the tide line in the left background in the 2.4 costume, with the long grey beard. Nagoji listens with thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, torn ochre tunic open over rope burns and cream dhoti, with no rope or irons. Flat grey overcast, black rocks, surf and the broken ship's boat. Hands and anatomy are sound, and there is no text. The open grey sky across the top band and between the Wary Fisherman and the Fisherman holds the three balloons clear of faces.

Acceptable with minor drift. (1) The Fisherman's white cloth sits on his near (RIGHT) shoulder, where 2.4 and 3.4 put it on his LEFT. Because he faces the other way from 3.4, this is barely noticeable. (2) The top-left background is a blocky grey stone outcrop, and the foreground has wooden barrels bound with rope. These read as jointed coastal rock and cargo washed up from the wreck, not a fort, but the shot is less of an open beach than 3.4. (3) Nagoji's hand bandages carry faint brownish grime stains; this reads as dirt, not fresh blood. The beat is right: the Fisherman leans in close at left with a hand at his chin, doing sums (grizzled grey beard, grey-streaked curls, bare head, cream vest, red lungi). Nagoji at right meets his eyes: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with only light stubble, small gold ear stud, torn ochre tunic open over rope burns, cream dhoti. His hands and wrists are wrapped in soaked, slipping bandages with the fingertips bare, which matches 3.4. The only forearm mark is a faint unreadable mottled patch. The sky is flat grey overcast with broken wreck timbers in the surf. There is no text, the hands are sound, and there are no painted balloons. Open sky across the top band and in the gap between the two heads holds the off-panel Wary line (tail out through the left edge, toward where he stood in 3.4) and the Fisherman's two lines, clear of both faces.

Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) The edit did not remove the small gold ear stud from the Fisherman, and the Young Fisherman also wears a gold drop at the ear. Both are tiny at page scale, and both men are clearly not Nagoji (grey beard; headband and chin beard). (2) The Wary Fisherman is a few paces off, but his head turns back toward the group rather than toward the palms. (3) Nagoji's hands are unbandaged, as in the earlier accepted takes. Everything else is clean. The flat grey storm sky and heaving grey-green surf now match page 3. The wreck is one high-sided dark hull with a carved stern castle and a snapped leaning mast. Nagoji is up on his right forearm with a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the gold stud, the torn ochre tunic, the cream dhoti and no irons. The brand on his LEFT forearm is pale raised wavy ridges with no letters, numerals or cross. The Fisherman crouches in a red lungi, cream vest and shoulder cloth. The Young Fisherman stands in an indigo lungi and headband, and the Wary Fisherman stands off with an off-white lungi and net. Hands are sound, there is no text and there are no painted boxes. Open grey sky in the upper centre (between the wreck and the Young Fisherman) and along the top-left holds Nagoji's balloon clear of every face.

Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) The Fisherman points south with his whole arm instead of jerking his chin; the beat still reads. Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) Nagoji sits upright with one knee raised and his left arm resting on it, rather than propped on one elbow as in 4.1 and 4.4. It is a patch of pale, raised, looping cord-like ridges, blurred past reading, with no legible letters, no numerals and no cross. The loops lean slightly script-like when zoomed, but they read as scar tissue at panel size. Everything else is clean. The relight now matches the page: grey overcast, grey-green foaming surf. The face matches the sheet, with a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin with only a stubble shadow, the small gold ear stud and long loose curls. Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) The wreck at right is a skeletal hulk with standing masts and tattered sail, not the carved-stern high-sided hull now shown in 4.1. It is small and at the frame edge. (2) The brand on Nagoji's LEFT forearm is a small pale ring-and-swirl mark on the upper side of the arm, rounder than the ridged patch in 4.1 and 4.3. It has no letters, no numerals and no cross, and it is tiny at page scale. (3) The Fisherman's raised brows are subtle, though his wide eyes and parted lips read as surprise. Everything else is clean. The relight matches 4.1 to 4.3 (grey overcast, grey-green surf, wet sand). The Fisherman matches 4.1 and 4.2: grey curls and beard, cream vest, shoulder cloth, checked red lungi, no ear stud. Nagoji is propped on his right forearm with chin lifted and shoulders squared. Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) Nagoji's dangling near arm (his RIGHT) has a small reddish mottled scrape mid-forearm. It reads as a fresh abrasion, not gore, but an attentive reader could take it for the brand on the wrong arm. (2) The Young Fisherman here has a moustache, a gold ear drop and a sleeveless indigo tunic. In 4.1 he wears a chin beard and a blue vest. The grinning Fisherman (white teeth, grey beard, cream vest, shoulder cloth, red lungi) holds Nagoji under the shoulders from behind. The Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) holds his legs at the knee and ankle. The Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, brown vest, net, long grey beard) walks ahead scanning the shore. Open sky at top centre, between the Fisherman's head and the Young Fisherman's head, holds both balloons clear of every face.

Minor only. The Wary Fisherman (net, off-white lungi) leads but also grips Nagoji's feet, and the Young Fisherman supports him under the thighs from behind, so the carry is shared three ways rather than strictly shoulders and legs. Minor only. The Wary Fisherman is not shown, which the script does not require. Some background roofs look tiled rather than thatched. The foreground girls wear short-sleeved tops. Minor. The girl in the far-left doorway is small and peeks from behind the door frame rather than clearly shrinking back. Acceptable, with notes. The brand on Nagoji's LEFT inner forearm (correct arm, facing camera) is a crisp raised-ridge scrolled monogram that suggests letterforms. It is not legible at any zoom, but it is sharper than the bible's 'blurred past reading'. The Woman stands just in front of the doorway rather than stepping out of it, and her red lips read slightly like lipstick rather than betel stain. The rope burns are raw red welts with no blood. She wipes her hands on her cloth and looks down at his arm. The Fisherman gestures and talks. Nagoji is on model: curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud. Both balloons fit in the sky at top left or over the thatch above her.

Acceptable, with notes. v06 is the v05 composition with the brand added, and it fixes the one gap v05 had: the brand now shows. Brand: a pale, puckered patch of raised ridges on the forearm he holds out to the Woman, which is his LEFT, about a hand's width above the wrist. It has no numerals and is not a cross. Its three ridge-strokes suggest letterforms (roughly 'L-c-u' when zoomed). At 1:1 and at print size they read as a burned-letter scar, not a word. This is the same level of letter suggestion as the scrolled monogram accepted in 5.4 v02, but the two shapes differ. The arm is turned so the brand sits more on the upper or thumb side than clearly on the inner side. The light is warm hearth light rather than 'cool'. There is a faint shadow under Nagoji's lower lip, within 'light stubble at most'. Everything else matches the beat. The interior is dim, with hearth smoke rising into the lit hole in the thatch. The ochre tunic lies peeled off in a pile on the woven mat. He wears the cream dhoti, and red rope burns cross his bare chest with no blood. The Woman has a grey-streaked low knot and undyed cotton over both shoulders, with no blouse and no gold. She washes his arm over a clay basin with his fingers hidden in her wet cloth, her mouth pulled tight. The Fisherman, in red lungi and shoulder cloth, squats at the mat's edge. Nagoji is on model: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear drop, no irons. Anatomy and hands are sound. No painted text, balloons or boxes. Lettering: the FISHERMAN balloon fits on the plain mud wall at upper left, beside and above his head. The NAGOJI balloon fits in the dark roof beams at top centre, between his hair and the smoke column. Both read left to right in script order.

Acceptable, with only minor deviations. Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with at most light stubble, small gold ear stud, long curly black hair, rope burns on his chest, tunic off, cream dhoti on, bandage on one forearm. The script beat is there. The Woman is wringing the cloth into a clay basin with her mouth open, speaking sharply. The Fisherman is in a red lungi with the white shoulder cloth on his own left shoulder, relaying her words with a half smile and a gesture. The setting is the same dim mud-walled, thatched interior with a hearth as 5.5. There is no text or pseudo-text in the art, and I checked the hands and feet at zoom: they are sound. The upper half (plain mud wall and thatch) gives plenty of clear space for both Fisherman balloons. Minor points: (1) the Woman seems to wear a sleeveless under-bodice beneath her draped cloth, which could read as a fitted blouse, against her 5.4 description; (2) Nagoji sits at mid-right, about level with the Woman, rather than clearly in the foreground; (3) the Woman looks toward the men instead of 'at no one in particular'. None of these is disqualifying. v08 was the only candidate offered.

Minor only. The boy is right: in the doorway, bare-chested with a towel on one shoulder, panting, one hand on the frame, backlit by grey light. The lamp is an open-wick lamp with no glass, the Fisherman (grizzled beard, red lungi, cloth on his LEFT shoulder) and the Young Fisherman (headband, indigo lungi) match, hands are sound, and there is no text. The plain dark upper wall has room for the boy's balloon (tail down-left to his mouth) and the caption. Deviations: the Fisherman looks at the boy rather than exchanging a look. The Young Fisherman's eyeline to the left passes through the Fisherman's face, so it reads as only half an exchange. Rain falls outside over paddy and the floor inside the door is puddled, which the script does not ask for. It also differs from the dry, sunlit doorways in the current 6.4 and 6.5 candidates, so those regenerations should use overcast grey daylight.

v06 is acceptable, with minor drift only. It is an edit of v03 that fixes the setting. The stone walls, sea, boats and hilltop fort are gone. It is now the mud-plastered, palm-thatched hut, and the open doorway shows palms and wet paddy in grey rain, which matches the 6.2 v07 and 6.4 v07 picks. The beat reads. The Fisherman (grizzled grey beard, cream vest, red lungi) crouches by the mat, looking down and speaking low. His right hand crosses his chest to adjust the white cloth on his own LEFT shoulder, and his hands are sound. Nagoji half-sits on the mat looking up at him. Nagoji matches the sheet and the chapter 4 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble, small gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, bare chest, cream dhoti and bandaged wrists, with no irons. The rope burns on his chest are reddish welts, not blood. Both his hands are anatomically sound, and the brand is not shown. There are no painted balloons, text or pseudo-text; the brass pot has only a faint floral chasing, no letters. The lamp has an open wick with no glass. Lettering space: the thatch band across the top left (x 0.0 to 0.5, y 0.0 to 0.18), the plain mud wall between the two heads (x 0.38 to 0.52, y 0.18 to 0.42), and the sky above the palms at top right (x 0.82 to 1.0, y 0.05 to 0.35). The long caption can sit along the top band or the bottom-left mat (x 0.0 to 0.5, y 0.88 to 1.0). Minor drift: (1) the red lungi has a faint check weave, whereas the script asks for plain dyed colour and the 6.2 and 6.4 lungis are plain; (2) the palette is warmer and sharper than 6.2; (3) the bandages cover only his wrists here, while 6.4 v07 wraps the whole hands.

Acceptable, with minor drift only. It fixes all three r4 failures of v05. Nagoji is bare-chested, as in 5.5, 6.1 and 6.3. Clean linen bandages cover his hands and wrists, and the cream dhoti is only salt-stained, with no rust or red blotches. The beat reads. Nagoji sits on the mat, eyes closed, with warm hearth light on his face. His face matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble, small gold ear stud and loose curly hair. The rope burns show on his chest, and he wears no irons. In soft focus behind him, the Fisherman (grizzled, cream vest, white shoulder cloth, red lungi) and the Young Fisherman (headband, blue vest, indigo lungi) turn their heads toward the doorway at right. A broad shadow of an unseen figure falls across the floor toward the mat. The hands are sound, and there is no text, noose or gore. Minor issues: (1) The narrow doorway strip at the right edge shows faint rain streaks, wet ground and grey surf beyond the palms. 6.5 v08 shows the same palms and sea but dry, with no rain, and 6.2 shows a dry village outside. The strip is small and soft at the frame edge, and a retouch to plain grey overcast would tidy it. (2) The brand sits on the upper side of the left forearm just above the bandage, nearer mid-forearm than a hand's width above the wrist. It is a patch of worm-like raised ridges, unreadable, with no numerals or cross. (3) The bandages run up to mid-forearm, longer than the wrist wraps in 6.1 and 6.3. (4) The out-of-focus Fisherman's cloth hangs over his right shoulder; 6.3 puts it on his left. (5) The frame is 3:2, but LAYOUT.json gives 6.4 a 100 pt row. Re-fit the row (fit-layout) rather than crop to a strip, which would lose the floor shadow and his hands; the script asks for a full-width tier, not a narrow strip. Lettering: the plain dark upper wall between Nagoji's head and the doorway (top 18 percent, x 30 to 85 percent) holds both captions clear of every face.

Acceptable, with minor drift. It fixes the earlier handedness failure. Nagoji half-reclines against rolled mats in the left foreground, chest toward camera, and looks straight up at the kapitan. His LEFT forearm, on the image-right side of his body, lies extended toward the kapitan, inner side up, with the bandaged hand palm up and five digits. The brand is on the inner forearm with no letters, numerals or cross. Nagoji matches his sheet and the bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, bare chest with rope burns, cream dhoti, bandaged hands and no irons. The kapitan has stepped well inside. He matches his sheet: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, a pale buttoned vest with pockets over a white shirt and white mundu, the blue-striped shawl, and no coat. He turns down toward image left, so his own left cheek faces the camera, and the thin scar runs from his left ear down into the beard. The Young Fisherman (headband, blue vest, indigo checked lungi) and the Fisherman (grey beard, cream vest, white shoulder cloth, red lungi) stand back behind him. The camera is low at mat level, looking up under the rafters. There is no text, noose or gore, and the hands are sound. Minor issues: (1) The doorway shows grey sea, beach and palms, while 6.2 shows a dry village outside. It does match 6.4 v07's doorway, apart from 6.4's rain. (2) The brand reads as a band of parallel horizontal ridges, closer to welts than to blurred burned letters. (3) Because the kapitan stands nearer the camera, 'shorter than the fishermen' does not read, though he is clearly broader. (4) His face is lit neutral-warm rather than strongly by the hearth. (5) Nagoji's thigh under the dhoti reads a little long against the shin of his extended leg, but the foot and ankle are sound. Lettering: the plain wall above and left of Nagoji (x 0 to 48 percent, y 0 to 24 percent, plus the wall at far left) and the plain woven floor band along the bottom (y 87 to 100 percent) hold all three captions clear of faces, hands and the brand.
